message:
Could Rohin’s report of child C2—predicting two formulas’ results, calculating a distinguishing case, and revising its judgment—help you compare your earlier flinch with this draft’s “afraid and excited”?
Would closer thought settle what the feather touch should reveal, or would a one-sentence revision provide better evidence?
What thinking or writing step do you choose to complete next?
What observation in the passage would make you change that choice?
What finding, uncertainty, and unfinished revision will you carry into the following turn, and which passage preserves your decision?
